title: Bob Vanderwarker (Bobby J. Van) | Obituaries | dnronline.com
text:
Bobby J. Van, previously known as Robert (Bob) W. Vanderwarker Jr., 89, of Harrisonburg, VA, peacefully left this world to be with his savior on Monday November 17, 2025.
He was born July 3, 1936 to Beatrice and Robert W. Vanderwarker Sr. in Fort Edward, NY.
He grew up in the Ticonderoga NY area with his younger brother Pete and sister Pam (the 3 Musketeers). He graduated from Ticonderoga High School where he was a multi-sport athlete and later inducted into their sports Hall of Fame. He earned his undergraduate degree from SUNY Brockport and Master’s degree from the University of Maryland.
Bobby loved sports. Whether he was playing, teaching, or coaching, he was in his element. He taught and coached soccer at the Maritime College and Hofstra University where he also coached baseball. Bobby and his family moved to Virginia in 1970 to take a position at Madison College, later known as JMU. He taught PE and Kinesiology until his retirement in 2001. He was also the Men's Soccer head coach from 1970 to 1987, where he took a fledgling program and built a powerhouse almost immediately. His teams won multiple Virginia State titles, and he was the first coach in any sport at Madison College to lead his team to an NCAA Division I tournament bid. Whether teaching or coaching, Coach V. made it his mission to make his students and players better people, preparing them for life, while making them better students and players. He was inducted into the JMU Sports Hall of fame in 2002. Coach Vanderwarker worked tirelessly with the recreation department to start the youth soccer program in Harrisonburg. He was also a world class college, professional and international soccer referee, a high school, NCAA, and professional basketball referee, and a Valley League baseball umpire. The community either loved or hated him depending on which way his last call went. He cherished his friendships and was eternally grateful for those who shared his joys and helped him through the difficult times.
When he wasn't coaching or refereeing you could probably find him at one of the local golf courses. He worked at each at one time or another (of course, in exchange for free playing privileges). He also relished the challenge of combing through the racing form to pick long-shot winners at the horse track. His favorite track was Saratoga. If not in any of the above places, he was likely traveling and being around famous athletes. Chauffeuring Jack Nicklaus and wife to the airport after his first US Open win; attending the World Cup in Germany in 1974; giving Sammy Sosa golf swing instruction at baseball Spring Training; or getting Cal Ripken or Alex Rodriguez to sign every item that he could pull out of his bag, pocket, or off his body. He, like his father, may call you from around the corner, or show up at your door, hoping for an offer for him to stay for a night or 2.
Bobby was preceded in death by his parents, his Aunt Bertha Drury VanCarpels (Aunt Bert), who greatly influenced his young life, his daughter Debbie Turner and his brother Pete Vanderwarker.
He is survived by his sister Pam Curtis and husband Cass of Granville, NY, son Tim and wife Betsy Vanderwarker of Huddleston, VA, daughter Laura and husband Mike Kerr of Jacksonville, FL, son-in-law Steve Turner and wife Ann of Harrisonburg, VA; 9 grandchildren, Logan Taylor and wife Ann, Kasey Watkins and husband Thomas, Alex Taylor, Will and Cole Click, Afton Vanderwarker, Morgan Dindinger, and Chandler and Cailyn Kerr; and 6 great-grandchildren, Mason Watkins, Maddox and Dakota McMillian and Adeline, Everett and Hazel Taylor.
No immediate services will be held. A celebration of Bobby's life will be held in Spring of 2026.
In lieu of flowers, please donate to a charity of your choice.
Online condolences may be made to the family by visiting www.mcmullenfh.com.
McMullen Funeral Home is in charge of arrangements.
